# Review: flaky-test fixes after the Vitest migration (commit `e22f39d49`)

Full review: all areas checked and both findings independently tested, with scope limited to the requested range. Nothing was modified, installed, run as a test suite or posted.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | ✅ Ready to open the PR |
| **Score** | **97 / 100** (2 of 2 findings checked) |
| **What held it back** | The `nameBuilder` fix has no test that fails reliably without it; two redundant `?.` |
| **Fix first** | Nothing blocks. Adding the test (finding 1) is the most useful follow-up. |

**Scope:** 63 files, +78 −70 · base `f6f3376` → `e22f39d` (committed only; one commit) · 60 files are the same `app.close()` → `app?.close()` swap in test teardown, and 3 have hand-written logic.
**Repo:** safe-client-gateway · TypeScript/NestJS · Vitest · Biome · 3 stated rules (AGENTS.md: layering, pre-commit checks, SPDX headers).

## Scores by area

| Area | Score | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Testing | 94 | Finding 1 |
| Simplicity | 97 | Finding 2 |
| Bugs | 100 | Both logic fixes are correct: trimming after the cut keeps names within the length limits, and the bridge-name resample loop ends quickly (20 bridge names vs a large noun list). |
| Regression | 100 | Test-only changes; `nameBuilder` is used only by test fixtures. |
| Conventions | 100 | All 63 changed files have the SPDX header. The swap covers every integration spec. |
| DRY | 100 | No new symbols or duplication. |
| Security · Architecture · Performance | n/a | Only test code and test builders changed; no new imports between modules, no queries or loops on request paths. |

**Not covered:** the 17 `*.e2e-spec.ts` files still use an unguarded `await app.close()`. They're outside this diff, so this is noted but not filed. No tests or linters were run, as you asked.

## Findings

**1 · Testing · P3 — the `nameBuilder` fix has no test that reliably fails without it**
`src/domain/common/entities/name.builder.ts:28` (the test that should guard it: `src/domain/common/entities/name.builder.spec.ts:13-20`)
- **What:** Running `sanitizeName` again after the 30-character cut is correct. But the only check is the random 50-run idempotence test, which is the same test that was flaking.
- **Why it matters:** One checker measured this against pinned faker 10.5.0: the bug only triggers when `faker.person.fullName()` is picked and lands a space exactly at the cut. That happens in about 1 in 1,400 test runs. A second checker simulated reverting line 28, and the suite failed in only 10 of 20,000 simulated runs (about 0.05%). So a revert would almost always go unnoticed until CI flakes again.
- **Fix:** Add one fixed-input test. Stub `faker.helpers.arrayElement` to return `() => 'A'.repeat(29) + ' Bcd'`, then assert `sanitizeName(nameBuilder()) === nameBuilder()` and that the result has no trailing space.
- **Checks:** confirmed and not refuted · confidence 55.

**2 · Simplicity · P3 — the bulk swap added a useless `?.` at two call sites that already checked `app`**
- `src/modules/chains/feature-flags/feature-flag.service.integration.spec.ts:23`: `if (app) await app?.close();`
- `src/modules/messages/routes/messages.controller.integration.spec.ts:49-50`: `if (app) { await app?.close(); }`
- **Why:** The `if (app)` check was already there, so the `?.` does nothing. Nothing can change `app` between the check and the call, and no lint rule requires it.
- **Fix:** Put back `app.close()` in these two places, or drop the `if` and keep only `app?.close()`.
- **Checks:** confirmed and not refuted · confidence 95.

## Your call

| # | Finding | Suggested |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fixed-input test for the cut-at-a-space case | Fix now: about 10 lines |
| 2 | Redundant `?.` in 2 files | Fix now: 2 lines, or skip |

## Worth tidying
- `src/modules/bridge/domain/entities/bridge-name.entity.ts:1` has no SPDX header. This diff only changed its spec file, so it's not a finding, but it's worth adding the next time that file is touched.

## Checked and ruled out
- A possible endless loop in the bridge-name resample at `bridge-name.entity.spec.ts:22`: the chance of drawing a bridge name repeatedly is negligible.
- `app?.close()` hiding real errors: when setup fails, Vitest still reports the setup error. The change only removes the misleading follow-on `TypeError` for every test in the file.

## How this was produced
- I ran the nine review areas myself instead of one agent per area, because the diff is small (about 150 lines, mostly one repeated swap).
- For each finding, one agent tried to confirm it and a second tried to disprove it, as independent checks.
- Nothing was written to `.git/safe-code-review/`, so the next run won't have a "since your last run" comparison.
